Understanding of data visualization tools and experience designing and building complex dashboards, including but not limited to Tableau, PowerBI, Qlik and similar. Analytics, statistics and/or database knowledge and experience (using tools, applications, platforms, etc.). Strong Project Management Skills: Overseeing complex, cross-functional projects, ensuring delivery on time and within budget. Collaboration: Ability to prioritize, and developing action plans. Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills. Title: Senior Data Analyst, DTC (Consumer & Ecommerce Analytics)

Description: Job Location: Mexico City, Mexico Calling all originals: At Levi Strauss & Co., you can be yourself — and be part of something bigger. We’re a company of people who like to forge our own path and leave the world better than we found it. Who believe that what makes us different makes us stronger. So add your voice. Make an impact. Find your fit — and your future. At Levi Strauss & Co, we are revolutionizing the apparel business and redefining the way denim is made. We are taking one of the world's most iconic brands into the next century: from creating machine learning-powered denim finishes to using block-chain for our factory workers' wellbeing, to building algorithms to better meet the needs of our consumers and optimize our supply chain. As a Senior Data Analyst you will be a senior individual contributor within the global Data, Analytics and AI team, turning ecommerce and consumer data into trusted, decision-ready insight for stakeholders across regions. You will own the definition, build-out, and governance of key metrics and dashboards — partnering with Product, Marketing, Finance, and Regional teams to make sure the business is steering on numbers it can trust. This role sits at the center of our analytics foundations: our data platform as the single source of truth, and the emerging semantic layer. In this role you will move fluently between SQL, the data warehouse, and visualization tools to answer business questions, build self-service products, and certify the definitions that everyone else consumes. You will raise the bar on data quality, consistency, and storytelling — and help establish the global-with-regional-voice governance model that lets local markets move fast without fragmenting the truth. You will be expected to mentor junior analysts, establish best practices, and contribute to the global Data, Analytics & AI community by sharing your knowledge and designing scalable, global solutions. About The Job Own key analytics workstreams end-to-end — from business question and metric definition through certified dashboard and adoption — partnering with stakeholders across the global organization. Define, certify, and govern metrics in the semantic layer and ARC, ensuring a single, consistent source of truth across ecommerce, consumer, and loyalty reporting. Build and maintain production-grade dashboards and data products (Looker, Looker Studio, Tableau, or similar) that drive self-service and reduce ad-hoc reporting load. Write complex, performant SQL against large datasets in BigQuery; build and maintain transformation pipelines (dbt) feeding the analytics layer. Act as the primary analytics point of contact for assigned business stakeholders — translating ambiguous business problems into clear analyses and communicating results to non-technical audiences with compelling data storytelling. Conduct deep-dive analyses (cohorting, funnel, CLV, retention, promo/discount, demand) to surface trends, quantify impact, and recommend action. Support experimentation and measurement — partnering on A/B test readouts, KPI alignment, and incrementality framing. Define and enforce best practices for metric documentation, dashboard standards, QA, and data validation within the team. Mentor and coach junior analysts, providing guidance on SQL, visualization, business framing, and career development. Drive global–regional analytics governance — aligning global frameworks with local market needs so regions get the nuance they need without forking definitions. Proactively identify data-quality, consistency, and readiness gaps, and partner with Data Engineering / Platform to close them. Ensure risks associated with deliverables are raised and mitigated to keep workstreams on track. About You Required Technical Skills: 5+ years of hands-on experience in data analytics, business intelligence, or a closely related field, delivering insight that changed business decisions. 5+ years writing complex SQL against large datasets in cloud-based environments; hands-on experience with BigQuery (or equivalent) and ideally dbt. 5+ years with data visualization / BI tools (Looker / LookML, Looker Studio, Tableau, or similar); able to choose the right visualization for the data and build compelling narratives. Strong grounding in metric definition and governance — building certified, reusable definitions rather than one-off reports; semantic-layer experience a strong plus. Solid analytical/statistical foundation — cohorting, segmentation, funnel analysis, retention/CLV, and a working understanding of experimentation (A/B testing, incrementality). Comfort with Python (or R) for analysis and automation. Experience with cloud data platforms, with a focus on Google Cloud Platform a plus. Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills; able to operate across regions and functions (Product, Marketing, Finance). Demonstrated experience mentoring junior analysts and establishing team standards. Desired Education And Experience Bachelor's or Master's degree in a quantitative discipline (statistics, mathematics, economics, computer science, data science, or related). Overall 5+ years of professional experience in analytics / business intelligence, ideally in retail, ecommerce, or consumer-facing industries. Track record of delivering analytics products (dashboards, definitions, deep dives) that drove measurable business impact (revenue, cost savings, decision quality). Prior experience as a senior individual contributor, with evidence of influencing team practices and stakeholder decisions. LOCATION Mexico, D.F., Mexico FULL TIME/PART TIME Full time Current LS&Co Employees, apply via your Workday account.

Title: Sustainable and Climate Finance Initiatives Consultant, Mexico
Description: Location: Mexico City: Mexico City Contract Type: Individual Consultant (Deliverable) Grade: Individual Consultant 4 Salary scale: Individual Consultant Scale End date of appointment From September 1 to December 31, 2026 Deadline: 15/08/2026 Job Reference: 100016501 Please note that the deadline is based on Korean Standard Time Zone (KST, UTC+9) INTRODUCTION TO GGGI The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page. General Information Project: MX34 Duty Station: Mexico City Contract Duration: September 1st – December 31st, 2026 Total Fees: 22,000 USD Consultant Level: Level 4 Project background Over the last decade, the Global Green Growth Institute has consolidated its role as a trusted advisor to Mexico’s federal and subnational governments, actively working collaboratively with key counterparts to establish a strong green growth foundation in the country. In 2014, the Mexican Senate ratified the Agreement for the Establishment of GGGI, which signals Mexico’s commitment to green growth and its recognition of the shared value of this development paradigm in cooperation with GGGI. In 2021, the Country Agreement between GGGI and Mexico was signed between the Mexican Foreign Affairs Secretariat and GGGI; hence, formally recognizing GGGI as one of the country’s key partnering international intergovernmental organizations. Mexico’s development priorities have evolved in the context of global and domestic changes, resulting in a significant push to transform the public life to achieve a greater benefit for all. This intent is ingrained in the National Development Plan 2025-2030, which serves as an umbrella for sectoral and institutional plans and a key tool for cooperation fostering inclusive development. The goal of its political, social, and economic pillars is to bring the nation toward prosperity, security, sustainability; thus, green growth and a low-carbon society are key development objectives for the country. Between 2019 and 2021, the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit of Mexico (SHCP for its acronym in Spanish) as National Designated Authority (NDA) of the Green Climate Fund (GCF), through the GCF Readiness Programme, has received funding to support activities that enhance and strengthen Mexico’s sustainable finance architecture to mobilize public and private, national, and international, climate financing for mitigation and adaptation projects and programmes in the country. In 2023, a Multiyear GCF Readiness Programme (MEX-RS-003) started its implementation to support the enhancement of Mexico’s priorities via Direct Access Entities and supporting the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (SHCP) in developing inputs that will allow the prioritization of projects based on national strategies and objectives in line with Mexico’s international climate commitments. Objectives of the Assignment The objective of this consultancy is to support the SHCP enhance its participation in international and bilateral initiatives and dialogues on climate finance by providing technical support to contribute to the achievement of Mexico’s international commitments while reinforcing its leadership in key climate forums. The consultancy will provide technical support to the strengthen SHCP’s participation in international climate meetings and events including those under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the Convention on Biological Diversity, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Council, the Coalition of Finance Ministers for Climate Action, the Regional Climate Change Platform of Ministries of Economy and Finance, among others, by preparing technical reports, strategic inputs and recommendations for SHCP’s positioning during its participation in these events, thereby strengthening Mexico’s access to international climate funds like the GCF. Scope of Work Role The Consultant will undertake the following activities related to the role of the SHCP as Mexico’s NDA to the GCF: Prepare and review technical inputs that will support SHCP in the implementation of the sustainable and climate finance agenda in the international initiatives and bilateral dialogues in which Mexico participates. Conduct research and develop reports on Mexico’s relations with foreign organizations in the areas of international fiscal affairs, sustainable finance, sustainable development, and climate finance. Prepare recommendations to strengthen the country’s position by identifying synergies between Mexico’s climate objectives and international and bilateral initiatives on fiscal affairs, sustainable finance, sustainable development, and climate finance. Follow up on bilateral collaborations based on Mexico’s climate finance objectives, as well as support SHCP in coordinating with internal administrative units to ensure compliance with national commitments. Systematize and report progress on Mexico’s international commitments and bilateral initiatives related to fiscal affairs, sustainable finance, sustainable development, and climate finance. Title: VP Credit Risk Review
Description: If you’re looking for a career where you can make a real impression, join our Global Service Center (GSC)- HSBC and discover how valued you’ll be. We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team in the role of VP Credit Risk Review Role purpose Credit Risk Review Examiners plan and conduct reviews of wholesale credit portfolios. Examiners examine in detail a representative sample of portfolio clients. For each reviewed client, examiners read relevant internal credit approval memoranda as well as the client’s public financial disclosures, press releases, external rating agency opinions, among other materials. Based on the information reviewed, examiners develop independent assessments of the appropriate risk rating for the reviewed clients and record their analyses and conclusions in a workpaper database. The examiners’ written analyses must be concise but thorough and may be subject to review by external bank examiners. Between formal reviews, Examiners independently monitor credit trends in individually assigned industry or geography-based wholesale portfolios and record their observations in monitoring journals. Credit Risk Review maintains an ongoing relationship with internal stakeholders responsible for credit approval, client credit management and credit policy. Examiners also interact periodically with external bank examiners. In addition to having a comprehensive understanding of credit analysis principles, Examiners should be broadly familiar with risk characteristics and exposure metrics for the array of credit products, including traditional loan products and securitization structures. Main Activities As examiner-in-charge, lead a team of Credit Risk Review officers in reviews of wholesale credit portfolios. This includes chairing all meetings associated with planning, initial kick-off, reviewing and presenting findings, and formal closing. It also includes coordinating the assembly of review files, ongoing communications with the business, reviewing workpapers written by other team members, drafting the final report, and supervising the archiving of all relevant documents. As examiner, participating in reviews led by other team members.
